Adjusted assessment using the Beige Book: The FOMC statement remains accommodative and notes a continued, albeit incomplete, recovery with subdued inflation. Beige Book insights around this period point to broad but uneven improvement across districts: manufacturing activity strengthened and many firms reported employment gains, with wage pressures concentrated in high-demand roles. At the same time, firms faced elevated pandemic-related operating costs (PPE, sanitation, testing, and remote-work technology), which squeezed margins and could temper hiring and investment. Balancing these Beige Book positives against SLOOS evidence of tighter lending standards and softer loan demand, the overall tone is slightly negative but less so than a credit-conditions-only read would imply.
